subject.title: fix: bind package-manager exec approvals to inner commands [AI]

question: Should this security hardening intentionally invalidate stale package-manager wrapper allow-always entries and bind durable trust only to parsed inner command targets?
rationale: The implementation direction matches the documented trust model, but it changes durable approval behavior for existing operators and defines a security-sensitive parser contract for package-manager wrappers.

options.title: Accept after live proof
options.body: Require a redacted live OpenClaw approval-flow transcript or logs, then merge the fail-closed hardening as the intended upgrade behavior.

options.title: Add upgrade messaging first
options.body: Keep the security fix but add an operator-facing release-note, doctor note, or migration explanation for stale outer-wrapper approvals before merge.

options.title: Pause for parser scope review
options.body: Hold the PR until maintainers decide exactly which npm, pnpm, yarn, npx, and bunx forms belong in the supported parser contract.

recommendation.title: Accept after live proof
recommendation.body: Require a redacted live OpenClaw approval-flow transcript or logs, then merge the fail-closed hardening as the intended upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice is closest to steipete's recent wrapper trust planning and realpath approval binding ownership history.
